name: Reference greenhouse
description: The reference scenario: 32 tomato plants in a small three-span house with fans, a heater on a thermostat, a dehumidifier, roof vents, sensors and a camera, from spring into summer under a season's weather, 120 days

notes.scenario: The reference scenario of P09 (reference-greenhouse-v1): modest enough to run on a laptop, complete enough to exercise every subsystem together. The viewer lists it first.
notes.envelope: Three 3.2 m spans, three 4 m bays, 4 m to the gutters: a small Venlo-style roof. A vent near each span's ridge, along the middle of the house, shut until commanded; a door in the front gable, by the path.
notes.layout: Four rows of eight plants along the house, 1.6 m apart about its middle, 0.75 m between plants, on gutters under two crop wires 3.6 m up, 30 cm either side of each row, a high-wire double row whose plants are trained to the wires by turns, with a pipe rail along each row; a path across the front. Its equipment, all off until commanded but for the heater, which its thermostat runs: two fans high over the front path blowing down the house, a 30 kW heater in the back right corner, sized to hold 16 °C inside on a freezing night, and a dehumidifier against the left side wall, halfway along. Its sensors: temperature and humidity at crop height in the front and back halves, the back pair imperfect (the back thermometer reads 0.5 °C high and drifts 0.001 °C an hour from the run's start, linearly and never recalibrated: an illustrative fault, not an ageing rate, about 9 °C a year where a healthy digital thermometer is specified to drift under 0.03 °C a year (Sensirion SHT3x-DIS datasheet); a failing or badly shielded sensor, made to stand out within a season, about 2 °C by the opening day and 3 °C by the season's end); an anemometer in the right fan's jet; CO2 in the middle; PAR in the canopy and under the roof; a camera at the front looking down the middle path; and a weather station 3 m in front of the house.
notes.crop_model: Organ by organ (P09.3): each plant a transplant of the plant lab's crop, its traits drawn from the seed, living each day in the house's mean air and its own light. The other scenarios keep the simple daily model.
notes.crop_work: Every week, a harvest round picks every red fruit, so that ripe fruit does not pile up and each plant's history lists what was picked from it; then a lowering round keeps each plant's top 30 cm or more under its wire, laying its bare lower stem down round its row's gutter, as a high-wire crop is lowered.
notes.start_date: 1 March, for 120 days: March's nights need heat, June's days need venting, and the crop bears red fruit for its last month or more.
notes.opening_day: Where the viewer opens it: the run's first day with red fruit, kept beside this manifest as a checkpoint (openings/reference_greenhouse.json.gz), so that its later days carry on from it rather than from the run's start. `python tests/test_opening_day.py --update` writes it again.
notes.random_seed: Seed 42, which the final QA resets to.
notes.climate: A cool, damp March night to start: 14 °C and 80% inside.
notes.weather: A season's weather (P10.3, the seasonal kind): each day's coldest and warmest temperatures follow the year at the site, from 0.5 and 5.5 °C on the year's coldest day, 20 January, to 13 and 22.5 °C half a year later, and wander from them in spells, 2.5 °C either way, a day keeping 0.7 of the day before's; each day its own clouds, 55% give or take 40. A day's shape and wind are the cold spring day's: coldest at 6 h, warmest at 15 h, a south-westerly veering to the north-west as it rises.
notes.daily: Its vents and fans by the clock, every day (P09.4): the roof vents half open at 9 h, fully from 11 h, half from 18 h and shut at 20 h; both fans from 8 h to 20 h. A fixed schedule cannot follow the season: from May the morning's sun warms the house before the vents open fully, and it passes 30 °C by 9 h on a bright day; a climate computer's venting setpoints would follow it.
notes.control: Its climate controller (P11), with its heating loop alone for now: the thermostat on its heater (P10.3), in place of daily commands to it, 18 °C from 7 h, 16 °C from 19 h, switching on below the setpoint by half a degree and off above it by as much. Its 30 kW hold the house at its setpoints through most of March, on and off as the air crosses its band, and run all night only on a freezing one; by June it runs on cool nights only. The vents keep their own clock, so on a cold day they let out heat the heater has to make up.
